Aulerci , ōrum, m., = Αὐλίρκιοι,
I.a people in Celtic Gaul, Liv. 5, 34, 5; acc. to Cæsar, divided into three branches.
I. Aulerci Eburovīces or Eburōnes (in Ptolem. Αὐλίρκιοι ʼΕβουραϊκοί), whose chief city was Mediolanum, now Dép. de l'Eure, in Normandy, Caes. B. G. 3, 17; Plin. 4, 18, 32, § 107.—
II. Aulerci Cenomani, now Dép. de la Sarthe, Caes. B. G. 7, 75; Plin. 4, 18, 32, § 107.—
III. Aulerci Brannovīces, now le Briennais, Caes. B. G. 7, 75.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
